title: Industry and Labor Leaders Deem Selic Rate Cut Timid
seoTitle: Brazil's Selic Rate Cut Seen as Timid
subtitle: A 0.25-percentage-point trim to the benchmark interest rate fails to satisfy productive sector and labor representatives
excerpt: A 0.25-percentage-point cut to the Selic rate was deemed insufficient by industry and labor groups, who argue the move fails to relieve economic pressure.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Brazil's benchmark interest rate, the Selic, was lowered by 0.25 percentage points, a move deemed insufficient by industry and labor representatives.

Organizations representing the industrial sector and the workforce labeled the decision timid, arguing that the cut falls short of delivering the expected relief to economic players.

According to statements released by these groups, the reduction fails to ease the persistent financial strain affecting various sectors of the economy.

With information from Agência Brasil.
